title: Reading Comprehension
notes: **Skimming and scanning.** Skimming reads quickly for the main idea; scanning searches the passage for a specific fact such as a date, name or number.
**Main idea and support.** The main idea is the point of the whole passage; supporting details explain, prove or illustrate it and usually answer factual questions.
**Inference.** An inferred answer is not stated outright — it combines stated details with the reader's reasoning to reveal what the writer implies.
**Vocabulary in context.** Unknown words are decoded from surrounding clues: synonyms, contrast words (but, however), examples and word roots.
**Answering strategy.** Read the questions first, locate the relevant paragraph, answer in your own words unless quoting is required, and check that every part of the question is answered.
